summary: Iteration 62 — Dev Chat v1 (Emergent-style collaborative dev inside chats): PASS end-to-end. 10/10 backend pytest cases green and full frontend smoke verified: POST /api/chats/dev creates chat (kind=development, bot_role_ids=['devmgr'], category='engineering') + linked dev_projects doc + 2 seed messages (ai-system welcome + ai-agent-devmgr intro). GET /api/chats/{id} returns kind/bot_role_ids/category/linked_dev_project. GET /api/dev-chat/roles returns exactly 14 rows (devmgr + dev group + 12 specialists) with required fields (key/trigger/label/desc/badge/color/is_group). Mention dispatch verified for @architect (sender_id=ai-agent-architect, body prefix '🏗️ **Architect** ·', metadata.role='architect'), @qa, @devmgr, and the @dev fan-out (all 8 dev roles arrive within ~60s). Kind guard verified: @architect in a normal group chat does NOT trigger any ai-agent reply. Frontend: New chat sheet shows 'Development project' with data-testid=new-chat-action-development; clicking calls POST /chats/dev and navigates to /chats/<id>. Split layout on ≥lg renders DevWorkspacePane with 5 tabs (dev-workspace-tab-plan/tasks/bugs/preview/memory) plus project header (name + v0.1.0 + 'stable' health pill). Tasks tab loads (empty state). MentionPopover in dev chat shows dev-role rows: typing '@arc' narrows to 'Architect @architect'; typing '@dev' shows 'Dev Manager @devmgr' and 'All developers @dev'. Composer placeholder exactly: 'Message New Development Project — type @ for AI · / for Dev OS'. MessageList renders 'Dev Manager' role label as sender name for ai-agent-devmgr messages.

issues: Radix warns: 'DialogContent requires a DialogTitle for accessibility' — wrap title in VisuallyHidden if visually hidden is desired. Non-blocking but pollutes console.

action_items: Optional: wrap DialogTitle in VisuallyHidden (or set aria-label) inside WhatsAppStyleNewChatSheet to silence Radix a11y warning.

Optional perf: parse_role_mentions returns the 8 dev roles for @dev — each then runs gpt-4o-mini sequentially via asyncio.create_task (which is parallel, good); however _gather_context() runs a full messages+project fetch per role (8× the same query). Cache once per dispatch and pass into post_agent_reply to cut Mongo load.
Optional: the @dev fan-out has no rate limiting — a malicious/spammy user can trigger 8 LLM calls per message. Consider per-user cooldown on dev fan-out (e.g., 1 fan-out per 60s).
critical_code_review_comments: services/dev_chat_agents.py:_gather_context is called once per role inside the fan-out loop, so @dev triggers 8× the same Mongo queries (messages.find + dev_projects.find_one). Compute once in maybe_handle_dev_chat_mentions and pass into post_agent_reply.

services/dev_chat_agents.py: post_agent_reply uses asyncio.create_task but never awaits/captures exceptions. If one LLM call hard-fails (not the caught Exception path), the task dies silently. Wrap in a try/log envelope at the task boundary.

services/dev_chat_agents.py: parse_role_mentions does NOT skip @-mentions inside code blocks or quoted text. A message like '`@architect`' or '> @architect' will still fire the agent. Minor but worth a follow-up.

routes/chats.py POST /chats/dev: project.plan only seeds 'product_brief' + '_llm_status'='stub'. The PlanView/DevWorkspacePane right pane reuses ProjectDetail tab components which may expect richer plan structure (pillars, etc.). Verified PLAN tab renders without errors (shows 'PRODUCT BRIEF' card), so it's safe — but consider seeding pillars too so the first-load experience is richer.

routes/chats.py POST /chats/dev: no rate-limit / dedupe — calling POST twice in quick succession will create two dev chats + two projects. Frontend currently navigates after the first response so it's fine, but consider returning the existing chat if one with identical name was created in the last N seconds by the same user.
test_credentials: amit@demo.team / Demo@2026 via POST /api/auth/demo-login (sets tn_session HttpOnly cookie).
seed_data_creation: Each run creates one TEST_iter62_dev_chat_<ts> dev chat (with linked dev_projects doc + 2 seed messages + N ai-agent replies) and one TEST_iter62_normal_<ts> regular group chat. These accumulate in the demo workspace; cleanup is non-destructive and prefix is searchable. Each @dev fan-out incurs 8 gpt-4o-mini calls — small token cost per run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend BASE_URL is read from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — export it when running pytest outside the kube pod. The full /api/chats/{id}/messages GET can be slow (>15s) when the LLM fan-out is mid-flight, so use timeout>=25s and tolerate ReadTimeout in poll loops (already handled in test_iteration62_dev_chat.py). The ai-agent reply message has sender_id='ai-agent-<role>' (note: 'devmgr' too), message_type='ai-agent', metadata.role=<role>, metadata.role_label=<Label>, parent_message_id=<trigger msg id> — those are the stable hooks. POST /api/chats/dev returns {chat, project}; the chat returned by POST has linked_dev_project attached inline while GET /api/chats/{id} attaches it from db.dev_projects via related_chat_id. Frontend testid map for the right pane: dev-workspace-pane, dev-workspace-tab-{plan|tasks|bugs|preview|memory}. New chat action: new-chat-action-development.
rca of the issue: No issues found. The Dev Chat v1 surface threads cleanly end-to-end: POST /chats/dev → chat+project+2 seed msgs → frontend split layout (left chat composer + messages, right DevWorkspacePane) → MentionPopover dev-role autocomplete → POST /chats/{id}/messages with @-mentions → maybe_handle_dev_chat_mentions (kind-guarded) → parse_role_mentions → asyncio.create_task(post_agent_reply) per role → LLM round (gpt-4o-mini via emergentintegrations + EMERGENT_LLM_KEY, with deterministic stub fallback) → db.messages.insert + _broadcast_message → MessageList renders ai-agent-<role> with role_label as sender name. All shape assertions hold even on stub fallback.
